rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A landlord may recover possession of a residential unit only by consent or through court eviction, and must have good cause to evict or fail to renew a lease. Each cause except nonpayment must be described in a written Notice to Quit (and sometimes a Notice to Cease), and a Judgment for Possession must be entered before the tenant must move.
rules.key_value: Warrant for possession not issuable until 3 business days after judgment; tenant then has 3 business days to move

requires.name: residential_rental
requires.text: applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied_small
exempt_if.text: two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units

exempt_if.name: transient_guest
exempt_if.text: hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant

exempt_if.name: family_trust_unit
exempt_if.text: a unit held in trust on behalf of a member of the immediate family who is developmentally disabled and permanently occupies the unit

coverage.summary: Applies to most residential rentals including houses, mobile homes, apartments and rooming/boarding homes.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Does not apply to certain small owner-occupied premises, transient or seasonal hotel/motel guests, and units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.

rules.quoted_span: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53). No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
